To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
Sp1 and SP3 are expressed in fetal and adult lung and interact with a 67-bps GC box sequence in the promoter of the ClC2 gene.
the Sp1 transcription factor activates ClC-2 transcription in fetal lung and that the downregulation of Sp1 in the postnatal period explains the perinatal down-regulation of ClC2 in the lung.
the Sp1 transcription factor is critical for ClC-2 transcription and that perinatal down-regulation of ClC2 in the lung is mediated by perinatal down regulation of Sp1.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the mechanisms of regulation of chloride-channel expression in airway epithelial cells.
the mechanisms that regulate the expression of a gene encoding a chloride channel that is critical to the normal development of the lung.
the molecular regulation of the Clc-2 chloride channel, a gene that is expressed abundantly in fetal lung and is important to the development of lung function in the perinatally period.

the Sp1 transcription factors are responsible for the perinatal regulation of ClC- 2 in the lung.
Sp1 and 3 are responsible for ClC-2 regulation during perinatal development.

perinatal down regulation of ClC- 2 is mediated by Sp transcription factors and that this downregulation is important to the maturation of the lung.
Sp1 and/or Sp3 transcription factors regulate ClC-2 transcription and that this regulation is critical for normal lung development.

the Sp1 transcription factor family members Sp1 and Sp1 are critical for the regulation of ClC- 2 expression during lung development.
